option.name: -Command
tip: Executes the specified command (and any parameters) as if they were typed at the Windows PowerShell command prompt, then exits unless NoExit is specified.
The value of Command can be "-", a string, or a script block.
If the value of Command is -, the command text is read from standard input.
Read command text from standard input.

option.name: -ConfigurationName
tip: Specifies the configuration endpoint that runs Windows PowerShell.
This can be any endpoint registered on the local computer, including the default Windows PowerShell remote endpoint or a custom endpoint with specific user role capabilities.

option.name: -EncodedArguments
tip: Accepts a Base64-encoded string version of command arguments.
Use this parameter to submit arguments that require complex, nested quoting.
The Base64 representation must be a UTF-16LE encoded string.

option.name: -EncodedCommand
tip: Accepts a command as a base-64 encoded string.
Use this parameter to submit commands to Windows PowerShell that require complex quoting or braces.

option.name: -ExecutionPolicy
tip: Sets the default execution policy for the current session and saves it in the $env:PSExecutionPolicyPreference environment variable.
This parameter does not change the execution policy set in the Windows PowerShell registry.
Valid values: AllSigned, Bypass, Default, RemoteSigned, Restricted, Undefined, Unrestricted.

next.name: AllSigned
tip: Only signed scripts run. Prompts before running scripts from untrusted publishers.

next.name: Bypass
tip: Nothing is blocked and there are no warnings or prompts.

next.name: Default
tip: Sets the default policy: RemoteSigned on Windows.

next.name: RemoteSigned
tip: Downloaded scripts must be signed. Local scripts run unsigned.

next.name: Restricted
tip: Permits individual commands but allows no scripts.

next.name: Undefined
tip: No execution policy is set in the current scope.

next.name: Unrestricted
tip: Unsigned scripts can run. Warns before running scripts from outside the local intranet zone.

option.name: -File
tip: Runs the specified script in the local scope (dot-sourced), so that the functions and variables created in the script are available in the current session.
Provide the script file path and any arguments.
File must be the last parameter in the command, as all characters following the File parameter name are interpreted as the script file path followed by script arguments.
An explicit boolean value for a switch parameter cannot be passed.
Read commands from standard input.

option.name: -InputFormat
tip: Describes the format of data sent to Windows PowerShell.
Valid values are "Text" (text strings) or "XML" (serialized CLIXML format).

option.name: -Mta
tip: Starts the shell using a multi-threaded apartment.

option.name: -NoExit
tip: Does not exit after running startup commands.

option.name: -NoLogo
tip: Hides the copyright banner at startup.

option.name: -NonInteractive
tip: Does not present an interactive prompt to the user.

option.name: -NoProfile
tip: Does not load Windows PowerShell profiles.

option.name: -OutputFormat
tip: Specifies how output from Windows PowerShell is formatted.
Valid values are "Text" (text strings) or "XML" (serialized CLIXML format).

option.name: -PSConsoleFile
tip: Loads the specified Windows PowerShell console file.
To create a console file, use Export-Console in Windows PowerShell.

option.name: -Sta
tip: Starts the shell using a single-threaded apartment.
Single-threaded apartment (STA) is the default.

option.name: -Version
tip: Starts the specified version of Windows PowerShell.
Provide a version number as an argument, such as "-version 2.0".

option.name: -WindowStyle
tip: Sets the display style of the Windows PowerShell window.
Valid values are Normal, Minimized, Maximized, and Hidden.

next.name: Hidden
tip: Hidden window

next.name: Maximized
tip: Maximized window

next.name: Minimized
tip: Minimized window

next.name: Normal
tip: Normal window

option.name: -WorkingDirectory
tip: Sets the working directory at the start of PowerShell given a valid PowerShell directory path.
Executing Set-Location -LiteralPath <path> at startup.
The current user's home directory.

global_option.name: -Help
tip: Show the help.
